summary: Radiation-induced correlated errors in transmon qubits are characterized using $^{241}$Am α-particles (5.5 MeV) and a pulsed 10–20 MeV electron linac, showing that gap engineering at both the Josephson junction ($δΔ_\mathrm{JJ}$) and capacitor/ground-plane interface ($δΔ_\mathrm{M1}$) mitigates but does not eliminate radiation sensitivity. A coupled quasiparticle dynamics model qualitatively reproduces the observed $T_1$, $T_2$, and transient frequency shifts across different gap profiles and junction orientations.
motivation: Recent QEC experiments observe a $10^{-10}$ error floor attributed to hadronic cosmic rays, and gap engineering at the JJ has reduced but not eliminated correlated errors; this work systematically characterizes radiation resilience across multiple gap profiles and energy scales to identify limiting mechanisms and design strategies.
method: Three transmon qubit arrays with different gap profiles (No-JJ-GE, JJ-Only with $δΔ_\mathrm{JJ}/h = 10$ GHz, and JJ&M1 with $δΔ_\mathrm{JJ}/h = 7$ GHz and $δΔ_\mathrm{M1}/h = 3$ GHz) were exposed to 5.5 MeV α-particles via collimated $^{241}$Am and to 14.5–1000 keV electron depositions at the CLIQUE facility, with heralded measurements of relaxation/excitation rates and Ramsey spectroscopy detecting transient frequency shifts and QP-driven state transitions.
result: Larger $δΔ_\mathrm{JJ}$ suppresses peak relaxation error rates (JJ-Only 3× lower than JJ&M1 at 145–435 keV), while larger $δΔ_\mathrm{M1}$ accelerates recovery by an order of magnitude for frequency shifts by trapping QPs in the base metal; sub-MeV radiation still causes detectable errors, and qubit temperature transiently reaches 175 mK with $∼100$ µs relaxation recovery and $∼1$ ms frequency-shift recovery in JJ-engineered devices.
